historical_references.reference: Rinku was an important queen of the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan region of ancient India. She is known for her role in securing the succession of her husband, Pravarasena II, to the throne after the assassination of their common father, Pravarasena I.

Rinku is also mentioned in early Jain literature as the wife of Mahavira Suri, the 14th Tirthankara of Jainism, indicating that she lived in the 12th or 13th century BC. The reference is found in the Bhagavati Sutra and describes her as a devoted follower of Mahavira Suri and a generous patron of Jain monasticism.
